scenario_prompt: Write the risk section of a solution proposal, naming each material risk and what is done about it, and stating plainly any risk that cannot be fully retired rather than omitting it. Context: the buyer's RFP requires a SOC 2 Type II report and the bidder holds only a SOC 2 Type I report today, with the Type II observation window closing after the RFP's submission date; separately, the bidder's own most comparable prior migration took 11 months, close to the buyer's 6-month compliance-audit deadline. Return only the risk section text.
text:
**Proposal section**

I have no discovery notes or RFP text supplied beyond the two facts given, so `PF-3.3` cannot fire on any term below; every term is judged by the deletion test alone. Two clarifying questions before this ships: (1) can the observation window be pulled forward or the audit scoped provisionally around the Type I report, and (2) what specifically differed in the prior 11-month migration that would make this one faster.

## Risks

**Compliance certification timing.** The buyer requires a SOC 2 Type II report. We hold a SOC 2 Type I report today. [PF-2.17 REVIEW (compliance): confirm current audit firm, Type I report date, and whether the Type II observation period can close before or shortly after RFP submission.] The Type II observation window closes after the submission date stated in this RFP. This is a real gap, not one we can close by submission: a Type II report cannot exist before its observation period ends. Our mitigation is to submit the Type I report together with a signed engagement letter from our audit firm confirming the Type II observation start date and expected report date, and to agree a contractual milestone requiring the Type II report before production go-live rather than before contract signature. [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): confirm we can commit contractually to a Type II delivery date tied to go-live rather than signature.]

**Migration schedule risk against the compliance-audit deadline.** The buyer's compliance-audit deadline is 6 months from contract start. [PF-1.14: buyer-stated deadline, this RFP.] Our most comparable prior migration took 11 months. [PF-2.2: source — our own delivery records for that engagement.] Adjacent evidence licenses this claim unhedged, so we state it plainly rather than softening it: at our demonstrated delivery rate, this timeline will not meet the buyer's 6-month deadline without a change to scope, phasing, or team allocation compared to that prior engagement. [PF-2.11 GAP: what specifically drove the 11-month duration on the prior migration — data volume, integration count, team size — has not been supplied, so we cannot state what a compressed plan would look like without inventing a new duration figure.] Our mitigation is to propose a phased cutover: the components the compliance audit actually depends on land first, on a schedule we will size once the gap above is closed, with the remaining migration continuing after the audit deadline under a separate, buyer-agreed timeline.

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| [PF-2.17 REVIEW (compliance): confirm current audit firm, Type I report date, and whether the Type II observation period can close before or shortly after RFP submission.] | PF-2.17 | Confirmation of audit firm, Type I date, and realistic Type II completion date |
| [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): confirm we can commit contractually to a Type II delivery date tied to go-live rather than signature.] | PF-2.14 | Internal sign-off on the go-live-linked delivery commitment |
| [PF-2.11 GAP: what specifically drove the 11-month duration on the prior migration — data volume, integration count, team size — has not been supplied, so we cannot state what a compressed plan would look like without inventing a new duration figure.] | PF-2.11 | Details of the prior migration's scope drivers, to size a credible phased plan against the 6-month deadline |
